newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 88 firm on Morrison bid.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 88 firm on Morrison bid.

text.p: Canadian 88 Energy Corp chief executive Greg Noval said on Monday his firm would not raise its bid for Morrison Petroleums Ltd should a competing offer surface.

"We won't be raising our bid," Noval said in an interview. "We're here for 21 days from mailing at 10 bucks a share and that's as far as we're going to go. We're not going to get into a public auction process."
Canadian 88 on Monday said it would offer C$10 cash or 1.5 Canadian 88 shares for Morrison, a much larger firm, in a proposed C$652 million deal.
Analysts have speculated that several Canadian energy companies could be rival bidders for Morrison.

Noval, who had yet to speak to Morrison executives, said the proposed merger would mean big benefits for both companies' shareholders. Morrison's stock has been out of favor since it reported disappointing drilling results from its Racehose Creek gas play in southwestern Alberta late last year.
"We like to pride ourselves where they've faltered and that's in finding and onstream costs," he said.

"Our three-year finding and onstream cost is C$4.12 a proven (barrel of oil equivalent), whereas if you pull out some historical statistics on Morrison you're going to see their costs up in that C$8 range."

Noval said that if the cash and stock deal was successful, cash flow from what would then be a senior producer would climb likely climb in 1997 to analyst projections of C$1.08 per share and earnings would also be positive.
Financing for the C$140 million cash portion of the deal would be provided by New York-based bank Chase Manhattan Corp, he said.
Following several recent asset sales, Morrison would have virtually no debt for Canadian 88 to acquire.

"We're debt-averse and this isn't a (leveraged buyout). A lot of these acquisitions are so loaded with debt that you don't want them after they're done. We're a focused company and we'll be at a magnitude where we've got a critical mass," Noval said.

He said that if the deal was successful, Canadian 88 would dispose of Morrison's 20 percent interest in North Sea explorer Morrison Middlefield Resources, but ensure that its facilities royalty trust, which was priced last week, was completed.
Noval said he was quite confident that Morrison announced its shareholder rights plan on Friday in anticipation of Canadian 88's offer on Monday.
